    <section class="prose-section" id="ai-adoption"><p class="eyebrow">QUT · Future Skills Organisation · 2025–2026</p><h2>Generative AI adoption by Australian workers</h2><p class="role">Principal Investigator &amp; Project Lead · $229,531 commissioned study</p><p>This national study examined how workers use generative AI and what support they need from employers. I led the study, coordinated the research team and working-group engagement, and helped develop the findings into resources for employers.</p><p>The work involved a <strong>41-member national AI Research Working Group representing 36 organisations</strong>, spanning government, unions, professional bodies, universities and employers of different sizes.</p><p>Working-group members represented organisations including the Digital Transformation Agency, National Artificial Intelligence Centre, Commonwealth Bank, Woolworths Group, Suncorp, Australian Council of Trade Unions, Australian Industry Group and the Council of Small Business Organisations Australia (COSBOA). <a href="https://www.futureskillsorganisation.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/AI-Research-Working-Group-Membership.pdf">See FSO’s published membership list ↗</a></p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Delivered</strong>A national research report, stakeholder workshops and co-design sessions, and an employer-support toolkit released as a working web application and downloadable resources for organisations building AI literacy, workforce capability and readiness.</p><a class="text-link" href="https://www.futureskillsorganisation.com.au/supporting-generative-ai-adoption-by-workers-the-role-of-employers/">Read the report &amp; explore the resources <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p><strong>QUT / ARC BITA:</strong> I led the team with Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan and Dr Stephen Whyte, with coordination and administrative support from Jen Petley.</p><p><strong>Future Skills Organisation:</strong> Michelle Circelli, Timothy Burt, Peta Skujins and the broader FSO team collaborated on the original project. Siobhan O’Sullivan has supported the subsequent stage and engagement with SMEs.</p></div></details><p>The research and employer-support resources have since informed further adaptation and SME engagement, including FSO’s <a href="https://www.futureskillsorganisation.com.au/sme-ai-coach/">SME AI Coach: download the resource pack ↗</a>.</p></section>
    <section class="prose-section" id="knowledge-platforms"><p class="eyebrow">QUT research collaborations · 2026–present</p><h2>Research software for archives and scientific interviews</h2><p class="role">Principal Investigator &amp; Project Lead</p><p>I lead two projects that help researchers search source material and check information extracted from it.</p><h3>Spanish Inquisition archival research platform</h3><p>With collaborators at QUT, the University of Oviedo and QUT eResearch, I’m developing software to search historical judicial records and extract information for analysis. I lead the project and supervise technical development. Extracted records retain links to the original documents so researchers can check them.</p><h3>Web of Stories scientometrics platform</h3><p>This platform lets researchers search interviews, videos and transcripts from prominent scientists. It links people and concepts across the material, helping researchers trace scientific relationships and the development of ideas.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Delivered</strong>Two access-controlled research applications deployed in QUT-supported environments, with workflows for structured extraction, retrieval and provenance-linked analysis. Access is managed within the research collaborations.</p><ul class="tag-list" aria-label="Methods"><li>Semantic retrieval</li><li>Knowledge graphs</li><li>Structured extraction</li><li>Human verification</li></ul><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p><strong>Both platforms:</strong> Tim Nguyen, an ARC BITA research assistant, undertakes the main software development under my supervision. The QUT / ARC BITA research team includes Professor Benno Torgler, Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan and Dr Douglas (Tony) Beatton, with deployment support from QUT eResearch.</p><p><strong>Spanish Inquisition project:</strong> international collaborators also include Professor David Matesanz Gómez (Universidad de Oviedo) and Andrea Teira Fachado (Universidade da Coruña).</p></div></details></section>
    <section class="prose-section" id="simulation"><p class="eyebrow">QUT · Queensland Department of the Premier and Cabinet · 2023–present</p><h2>Behavioural simulation for public decisions</h2><p class="role">Chief Investigator &amp; Project Lead</p><p>I lead research and stakeholder engagement on combining synthetic populations, behavioural evidence and agent-based modelling to investigate vulnerability, resilience and decisions in disaster management and crime prevention.</p><p>My responsibilities include MPhil supervision, technical coordination and engagement with government and industry research partners.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Delivered</strong>Applied AI and behavioural-simulation platform development, with research demonstrations delivered in April 2026.</p><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>Arian Mashhady, an ARC BITA / QUT MPhil student, undertakes the main software development and research under supervision from me, Professor Benno Torgler and Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan, with additional support from Dr Douglas (Tony) Beatton.</p></div></details></section>
    <section class="prose-section" id="other-research"><p class="eyebrow">Government, industry &amp; university collaborations</p><h2>Evidence for policy and practice</h2><h3>Drivers of AI Investment · IP Australia</h3><p>Co-author of a 2023 commissioned study connecting workforce skills, job advertisements and patenting activity to investigate AI investment and innovation.</p><p><a href="https://www.ipaustralia.gov.au/tools-and-research/professional-resources/data-research-and-reports/publications-and-reports/drivers-of-ai-investment">Read the published IP Australia report ↗</a></p><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>The research team comprised Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan, Professor Uwe Dulleck, Professor Benno Torgler and me, with partner support from Annita Nugent and Michael Falk at IP Australia.</p></div></details><h3>RiskWise · AI-assisted qualitative analysis</h3><p>As Applied AI Research Lead, I led conceptual design and contributed to technical development of a workflow for scalable, traceable qualitative coding. It combines semantic automation, language models, human review and provenance-linked outputs, and has been applied to <strong>more than 4,250 Australian agricultural research, conference and extension artefacts</strong>.</p><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>With Tim Nguyen and Dr Germán Puga and Professor Marit Kragt at the University of Western Australia.</p></div></details><h3>AI copilots, work and professional identity</h3><p>I lead a QUT ethics-approved longitudinal study, developed with Inspired Education Group, examining how enterprise AI copilots affect work practices, capability, identity, trust and collaboration in Queensland high schools.</p><p><a href="publications.html">Browse related research outputs →</a></p><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p><strong>Study in progress:</strong> Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan, Professor Benno Torgler, Dr Douglas (Tony) Beatton, Arian Mashhady and me at QUT / ARC BITA, working primarily with Rashan Senanayake at Inspired Education Australia.</p></div></details></section>
    <section class="prose-section" id="surveylm"><p class="eyebrow">Panalogy Lab · Independent applied AI R&amp;D · 2023–present</p><h2>SurveyLM</h2><p class="role">Co-Creator &amp; Research Lead</p><p>I co-created a platform for constructing configurable synthetic populations and running model-based experiments on attitudes, values, preferences and decisions. The work combines structured data generation, cross-model comparisons and statistical analysis.</p><p>I lead the research and experimental design, contribute to development and coordinate the platform’s requirements. Much of my work tests its responses against human evidence and examines where the results depend on modelling choices.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Delivered</strong>A research platform, a public technical report and peer-reviewed validation research comparing human and synthetic data in service-failure and recovery settings.</p><p><a href="https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2308.00521">Technical report ↗</a> &nbsp;·&nbsp; <a href="https://doi.org/10.1108/JSM-11-2023-0441">Peer-reviewed study ↗</a></p><p class="note">I presented our augmented language model work and showcased Panalogy Lab at Something Tech / Something Fest in Brisbane in 2023.</p>

    <section class="prose-section" id="industrial-ai"><p class="eyebrow">Panalogy Lab · Industrial applications</p><h2>Industrial and physical AI</h2><h3>Agent Rung · Industrial control intelligence</h3><p>An industrial fault-diagnosis and decision-support system combining live PLC data, vendor-specific knowledge and safety-oriented reasoning. The system has been deployed at industrial sites in Australia.</p><p><strong>My contribution:</strong> defining industrial use cases and requirements with engineering partners, and coordinating deployment with the technical team.</p><h3>Icebreaker · Virtual production supervisor</h3><p>A manufacturing decision-support system combining production-line modelling, a language-model reasoning agent and natural-language queries of production data. Initial pilot work focused on a food and beverage manufacturing plant on the Gold Coast.</p><p><strong>My contribution:</strong> scoping the project with the industry partner, defining operational requirements and coordinating the engineering and software work. Pilot findings are context-specific; broader deployment remains under development.</p><h3>GAIA / Expert Recommender</h3><p>Related knowledge-system applications combine document intelligence, structured extraction, semantic search, knowledge graphs and expert-recommendation workflows.</p><a class="text-link" href="https://panalogy.ai/">Explore Panalogy Lab <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p><strong>Agent Rung and Icebreaker:</strong> primarily with Dr Son Tran and Latzi Marian at Panalogy Lab.</p><p><strong>GAIA:</strong> developed with the broader Panalogy Lab team, particularly Dr Son Tran and me.</p><p><strong>Expert Recommender:</strong> primarily with Dr Ho Fai (Ben) Chan, Professor Benno Torgler and an intern I supervise, within the broader Panalogy Lab team.</p></div></details><p><a href="https://panalogy.ai/technology">Panalogy Lab technologies ↗</a> &nbsp;·&nbsp; <a href="https://panalogy.ai/case-studies">Applications and case studies ↗</a></p></section>
    <section class="prose-section" id="readiness"><p class="eyebrow">Panalogy Lab · Verbrec · 2025</p><h2>Organisational AI readiness</h2><p class="role">Project Lead</p><p>I led an AI-readiness and requirements study across a multi-site, multi-team engineering services organisation, with contributions from across the Panalogy Lab team. The work covered requirements gathering, use-case prioritisation, business cases, project planning, and cost and schedule estimates to support decisions about introducing AI.</p><p class="deliverable"><strong>Delivered</strong>An organisational readiness assessment and requirements-scoping study to support decisions about where and how to introduce AI.</p><details class="project-credits"><summary>Team &amp; collaborators</summary><div><p>Led by me with contributions from the broader Panalogy Lab team, working with staff and leadership at Verbrec.</p></div></details></section>
